nodes.question: What future mechanism does the research propose to monitor the effectiveness of energy optimization measures?
nodes.answer: The research proposes establishing a long-term monitoring mechanism to continuously track residential buildings after adopting optimization measures to evaluate their actual effect.
nodes.paragraph: With perspective focusing on the special regional and ethnic characteristics of the plateau, this research aims to promote energy conservation and sustainable development of local traditional buildings of ethnic minorities, and help improve the living environment of the Sichuan Plateau. nodes.question: How did the Scarcity Malaga project in Spain reduce electricity consumption?
nodes.answer: The Scarcity Malaga project in Spain reduced electricity consumption by 25% through efficiency improvements and the integration of demand monitoring and management systems.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What indicators are used in the LED Analysis to prioritize inventory?
nodes.answer: The LED Analysis uses consumption value as the basis for a production schedule and also considers inventory movement and sales as performance indicators to prioritize inventory effectively.

nodes.question: According to the paragraph, what do smart energy apps provide to users?
nodes.answer: They offer context-specific feedback that allows users to track and reflect on their consumption patterns.
nodes.paragraph: "Discussions" discusses the findings. Sect. "Limitations and Further Research" outlines the study S limitations and proposes direc- tions for future research. Finally, Sect. "Conclusion" summarizes the findings and broader implications for the field. Background App-based energy feedback and user engagement App-based energy feedback has emerged as a prom- ising digital solution to enhance user awareness and engagement with energy usage. A systematic review by Chatzigeorgiou and Andreou, (2021) examined feedback research for residential energy behaviours Energy Efficiency (2025) 18:25 25 Vol. : (123456789) through mobile and web interfaces, highlighting the need for more comprehensive studies on these solu- tions long-term impacts and scalability. Smart energy apps offer context-specific feed- back that allows users to track and reflect on their consumption patterns (Hermsen et al., 2016). This feedback can assist users in exploring manage- ment strategies, yet the extent to which these apps shape sustainable energy practices within house- holds remains under-researched and still limited to pilot-level projects (Attour et al., 2020; Geelen et al., 2019; Murugesan et al., 2015; Valor et al., 2019).
